text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Thursday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Riga hosts the 6th session of the Baltic sea council, attended by foreign ministers from nine countries. Discussions will focus on co-operation in fighting against organized crime, as well as environmental and economic co-operation.

- Next week will be critical for Transport Minister Vilis Krishtopans since the prosecutor's office has told the press that information about his possible breaching of the anti-corruption law would be made public next Monday.
- Russia decided to recognise Latvia's non-citizen passports as valid documents for entering the country.
- The board of Latvia's Farmers Union nominated Irena Folkmane to the post of minister of culture.
- The Washington correspondent of Diena reports that the U.S. press has recently been paying much attention to issues of Baltic security.
- Latvian company Latelektro signed a contract with German firm SiKom to invest 25 million marks in building co-generation power stations in Latvia's small towns.
- Trasta komercbanka is to launch on July 7 the first issue of public shares from insurance company Balta.

- The prosecutor's office has finalised its report on Prime Minister Andris Shkele and his activities in various companies. It will be made public after being approved by the constitution protection bureau.

- The Bank of Latvia at its monthly press conference said the bank system has entered a period of stability. Central bank chief Einar Repshe urged Latvians to use lats instead dollars to avoid false banknotes. Over the last six months, the bank has bought about $20 million to prevent the lat from rising.
